incidents.cause: The pilot’s loss of directional control during the landing roll.

The pilot's inadequate in-flight decision by failing to refuel while en route, resulting in fuel exhaustion.    Contributing to the accident were a proper touchdown point was not possible and the inadequate display of the fuel quantity indicator.
The pilot’s failure to maintain airplane control, which resulted in pilot-induced oscillations and a subsequent loss of control and impact with terrain.
The pilot’s failure to maintain a proper glide path during the final approach, resulting in a collision with the airport approach lights.
The pilot’s failure to maintain airplane control during a go-around from unsuitable terrain.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of experience in the make and model airplane.
The pilot's selection of unsuitable terrain for landing, resulting in the airplane nosing over during taxi.
The pilot’s failure to maintain adequate clearance from terrain during low-level maneuvering.
the failure of the ground operations personnel to maintain awareness of the relative position of the two airplanes.

The failure of the tug operator and wing walker to adequately monitor the environment during pushback of the airplane from the gate in preparation for flight, which led to the collision of the airplane with an adjacently parked airplane.

The pilot’s initiation of the visual flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in spatial disorientation and a subsequent loss of helicopter control. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s flicker vertigo during the flight.

The pilot's inadequate recovery from a loss of tail rotor effectiveness during a low altitude downwind hover in a gusty wind condition resulting in the helicopter contacting the ground and rolling over.
A loss of hydraulic fluid due to a fractured left main landing gear hydraulic actuator as a result of a fatigue crack, which led to the landing gear collapsing upon touchdown.

A loss of hydraulic fluid due to a fatigue failure of the right main landing gear hydraulic actuator, which resulted in the pilot's inability to fully extend the landing gear and a main landing gear collapse during the landing roll.
